steps.title: Prepare all solutions
steps.instruction: Make fresh staining, washing, and storage solutions using the recipes below and keep them at the indicated temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Staining solution (20 mL total): dissolve 20 mg DAB (1 mg mL⁻¹) in deionized water, add 16 µL 37 % HCl (final 8 mM, pH ≈ 3.8), stir vigorously at room temperature protected from light for at least 2 h until clear to very light brown; store at 4 °C for up to 2 days.

Washing solution (50 mL total): mix ethanol, lactic acid, and glycerol in a 3:1:1 volumetric ratio to obtain 60 % (v/v) ethanol, 20 % (v/v) lactic acid, and 20 % (v/v) glycerol; store at room temperature in a sealed container for up to 6 months.

Storage solution (50 mL total): mix glycerol and water to obtain 60 % (v/v) glycerol (30 mL glycerol + 20 mL water); store at room temperature for up to 2 years, and keep mounted samples at 4 °C for 7–10 days before fungal growth appears.

steps.title: Add staining solution to wells
steps.instruction: In a 6‑ or 12‑well plate add 1 mL of the freshly prepared staining solution to each well that will contain seedlings, ensuring the well bottom is fully covered.

steps.title: Transfer seedlings into wells
steps.instruction: Using tweezers gently place 3–5 seven‑day‑old (or 3–7‑day‑old) Arabidopsis seedlings into each well, keeping different genotypes or treatments in separate wells to avoid mixing during incubation.

steps.title: Vacuum infiltrate seedlings
steps.instruction: Cover the plate, place it in a vacuum chamber, and apply a pressure of –67 kPa (‑500 mmHg, ‑20 inHg) for 5 min; release pressure slowly, swirl the plate, and repeat for a total of two infiltration cycles.

substeps.instruction: Secure the lid with a heavy metal weight or tape to prevent spillage.
If a manometer is unavailable, verify a tight seal by gently lifting the chamber before timing.
For oil‑based pumps, allow air to re‑enter slowly before disconnecting.

steps.title: Incubate staining in dark
steps.instruction: Wrap the plate completely in aluminum foil and incubate at room temperature on an orbital shaker set to 80 rpm for 15 min; adjust rpm if the shaker orbit differs from 25 mm to maintain gentle mixing.

steps.title: Discard staining solution
steps.instruction: Gently pipette out the staining solution from each well without aspirating the roots; from this point onward samples may be handled under normal light.

steps.title: Wash seedlings
steps.instruction: Perform three washing cycles with the washing solution to remove excess DAB precipitate.

substeps.instruction: Optional pre‑wash: add 1 mL washing solution, swirl, and discard.
Add 1 mL fresh washing solution, swirl gently, then discard.
Incubate at room temperature on the orbital shaker (80 rpm) for 10 min.
Repeat the add‑incubate‑discard sequence two more times (total three cycles).

steps.title: Add storage solution
steps.instruction: Replace the washing solution with 1 mL of storage solution in each well; plates can be stored at 4 °C for up to one week (longer if no fungal growth is observed).

steps.title: Mount roots for imaging
steps.instruction: Detach roots just below the hypocotyl‑root junction (or use a small 20 × 20 mm coverslip for intact seedlings), place 20–50 µL drops of deionized water on a glass slide spaced ~0.5 cm apart, blot excess glycerol, position each root in a drop, cover with a coverslip, and add extra water if needed.

substeps.instruction: Do not mount roots from different experimental categories on the same slide to avoid mixing.
If roots are detached, transfer them to the water drops after cutting with a scalpel.

steps.title: Acquire brightfield images
steps.instruction: Using a transmitted‑light microscope, capture single‑plane brightfield images of the root apical meristem, elongation zone, and part of the differentiation zone with consistent illumination intensity, gain, and exposure to avoid saturation.

steps.title: Prepare images in FIJI
steps.instruction: Open each image in FIJI, convert to RGB Color (via Bio‑Formats Importer for multi‑channel files or Image > Type > RGB Color for standard files), and rotate the root vertically.

substeps.instruction: If direct RGB conversion fails, first convert to 8‑bit then to RGB.

steps.title: Separate DAB signal
steps.instruction: Apply Colour Deconvolution with the ‘H DAB’ vector to generate three 8‑bit images; keep the original RGB brightfield image and the Colour 2 (DAB) image for analysis.

steps.title: Define ROI and quantify
steps.instruction: Draw a horizontal rectangular ROI (wider than tall) on the brightfield image covering the root region of interest, add it to the ROI Manager, transfer it to the Colour 2 image, then quantify DAB intensity.

substeps.instruction: Select the ROI in the Colour 2 window, then choose Analyze > Gels > Select First Lane and Analyze > Gels > Plot Lanes.
Draw a baseline at the peak base with the Straight Line tool, use the Wand tool to click inside the peak, and record the enclosed area (integrated intensity).
Ensure the peak is not truncated at the top; truncation indicates saturation.

steps.title: Optional visualisation of intensity
steps.instruction: Create a qualitative colour map of DAB intensity using the Spectrum LUT.

substeps.instruction: Convert the image to 8‑bit, then apply Image > Lookup Tables > Spectrum.
Adjust brightness/contrast uniformly across all images (Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast > Set) and propagate the settings.
Save the visualised image as JPEG or another desired format.
